record.paper_title: Major Unsolved Problems in Space Plasma Physics
record.original_question: For proton cyclotron waves in low-beta space plasmas, do nonlinear or coarse-grained fluid treatments of resonant wave-particle interaction change the expected damping enough that ion-cyclotron waves in the solar corona may survive longer than linear theory predicts, thereby requiring reevaluation of linear ion-cyclotron damping scenarios?

evidence.quote: Much still needs to be done in this area
ion cyclotron waves may not damp as rapidly as predicted by linear theory.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a collisionless, low-beta (plasma beta β ≪ 1) magnetized plasma intended to model conditions in the solar corona, consisting of protons and electrons in a background magnetic field B₀. Let proton cyclotron (ion-cyclotron) waves propagate (quasi-)parallel to B₀ at frequencies near the proton gyrofrequency Ω_p = eB₀/m_p c. Linear Vlasov–Maxwell theory applied to a Maxwellian proton distribution predicts a cyclotron-resonant damping rate γ_lin > 0 due to wave–particle interaction at the resonance v_∥ = (ω − Ω_p)/k_∥.

Develop a rigorous nonlinear or coarse-grained fluid/kinetic treatment of resonant wave–particle interaction for this system (for example, by including finite-amplitude trapping, quasilinear plateau formation along curved diffusion shells in velocity space, or a coarse-grained fluid closure that retains the dominant resonant physics), and determine whether the effective damping rate γ_eff produced by such a treatment satisfies γ_eff < γ_lin by an amount sufficient to make the wave-energy decay length L_eff = v_g / γ_eff comparable to or larger than the coronal heating scale heights of interest.

The problem is: prove or disprove that nonlinear or coarse-grained treatments of cyclotron-resonant wave–particle interaction in such low-beta plasmas yield a sufficiently reduced effective damping rate that proton cyclotron waves can persist in the solar corona over scales substantially exceeding those predicted by linear theory, thereby requiring a quantitative reevaluation of linear ion-cyclotron damping scenarios.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature continues to actively investigate cyclotron damping of waves in the solar corona, including non-Maxwellian distributions, quasilinear shell diffusion, and turbulence cascade limitations. No consensus result has emerged showing that nonlinear/coarse-grained treatments definitively rescue ion-cyclotron waves from rapid linear damping; the problem of whether such effects substantially extend wave survival in the corona remains under investigation.

status_evidence.snippet: Discusses ongoing challenges in modeling ion-cyclotron resonance and parallel cascade in the corona.
status_evidence.claim: Ion-cyclotron damping versus cascade replenishment remains an open modeling issue.

status_evidence.title: A study of particle acceleration... in non-Maxwellian coronal plasma
status_evidence.snippet: Examines damping length of kinetic Alfvén-related waves in non-Maxwellian coronal plasmas.
status_evidence.claim: Nonlinear/non-Maxwellian effects on wave damping are actively investigated, with no settled answer.

status_evidence.title: Wave dissipation by ion cyclotron resonance in the solar corona
status_evidence.snippet: Standard linear cyclotron-resonance dissipation analyses underpin current heating models.
status_evidence.claim: Linear theory remains the baseline; nonlinear modifications are not yet conclusively established.
